To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Note on the Seller's preamble:** The Seller says its positions were "settled at principal level", are "FINAL" and reflect "standard market terms". That is the Seller's own assertion and is not authority. We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback on this draft. Its labels should not move any position below. Every item stays open for mark-up.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Clause 12.1 caps general Warranty Claims at 20% (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and we have none.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once it is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 on a first-dollar (tipping) basis.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and an excess-only basket permanently removes the first AUD 250,000 of recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. The Seller also wants every limitation to apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The default wording is a hidden override (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, a claims period of at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranties regime.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so they cannot share a 20%/18-month cap.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express overriding fraud carve-out in each clause.** This is non-negotiable under the playbook and cannot be waived by anyone.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 disclose the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. Accept only the specific disclosures in paragraphs 2 to 10, and only to the extent they are fair and specific.** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure moves diligence risk onto the Buyer and empties the warranties. Paragraph 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable, but it must not dilute fairness.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars any claim for matters known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete clause 8.3.** If any qualifier survives, it should be the Seller's knowledge only, limited to named persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. The "discoverable" limb in particular would duplicate deemed disclosure and remove protection the warranties are meant to give.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (paragraph 2) confirms no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, both as a Condition Precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent a CP, with supporting evidence delivered.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m), so consent on delivery plus reasonable endeavours is inadequate for a customer this material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter paragraph 3 confirms the facility (about AUD 3.2m) is unpaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a payout letter, a direct funds-flow payment to Riverlark, and executed releases delivered at Completion.** A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item (treated as a Debt-like or Transaction Expense deduction) or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add an express line item or a Seller-funded mechanism, plus an indemnity for the bonuses and on-costs.** As drafted, the funds flow silently leaves the Company, and therefore the Buyer, paying them.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The clause 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering loss from any failure to vest or assign the Ironquay Project Materials, with the SOW3 cure preserved.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity. Keep the SOW3 payment cure and require a confirmatory assignment at or before Completion.** Treat the AUD 180,000 in DD-010 as unverified in both directions (it is neither confirmed owing nor confirmed paid), and keep the indemnity outside the general cap and basket.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a continuing investigation, and regular updates to the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** **Add covenants to preserve logs, continue the investigation, give the Buyer updates and access, and obtain Buyer consultation before any notification decision. Back this with a specific indemnity.** Our current position is that there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation nor assert a breach or numeric claim.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment before agreeing to any treatment.
- **Recommendation:** **Assess first.** Request information on timing, terminability, accrual and whether the renewals are ordinary course (DD-008 and DD-011 read together). Do not pre-classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction at this stage. The Disclosure Letter itself does not state their nature, so the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported, but so is any automatic deduction.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (clause 12.3/13), limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5), and Tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as distinct categories, with no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the catch-all wording. Draft each category's limitations expressly, and make general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.** The current drafting quietly applies the general cap to every category.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter paragraph 10 itself concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Require independent evidence** of title, encumbrances and authority, for example ASIC and PPSR searches, share certificates, constitution and board approvals, and evidence of authority to sell. DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** These terms to remain open.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN. Do not accept them as settled, and do not concede the general cap for these categories.** No resolution has been reached. Equally, we should not assume or demand unlimited liability; the regime for each is still to be negotiated.

---

**Summary:** None of the Seller's positions is acceptable as drafted. The priorities for the mark-up are:
- the fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005);
- the Fundamental/Title regime (SPA-N-004);
- Bluefen as a CP (SPA-N-008);
- the Riverlark payout at Completion (SPA-N-009);
- the bonus line item (SPA-N-010);
- removing deemed disclosure and the buyer-knowledge bar (SPA-N-006 and SPA-N-007).

No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, or a post-Completion Riverlark release) should be offered without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
